Corrected earlier inference about duplicate validations. Persisted execution a20c9528-c2da-4458-934f-bc1e58284b3b for incoming h1scc59a7pfmjxshoyi9cmea5w has ONE attach_documents tool invocation (call_2ee471a7da744eab917add51d48e3ba0) and one tool result, despite two Channels validations at18:21:05.322 and05.608. Source confirms AttachDocuments validates once per run; Jido.Exec default allows1 retry with250ms backoff, and Jido.Error.retryable? treats unclassified tuple errors as retryable. file_too_large is such a tuple. Therefore the repeat is execution-layer retry inside one model tool call, not two model decisions or duplicate shared delivery execution. No retry-policy changes made.

ZAQ maps upload_then_publish and max_upload_request_bytes::unresolved with native threads/attachment edits, validation fails stageconfiguration/not_sent. Continue collapses14 files to an attachment-free streamed edit, confirmed227ms, reportpartial with indices0..13 failed. Thus independent missing upload-request byte ceiling is proven, hardcoded10-file count is valid; no uploads attempted. No settings or failure-policy changes made.

Provider-vs-host distinction verified after user challenge. Mattermost official environment docs specify FileSettings.MaxFileSize and separate deployment proxy limits (NGINX client_max_body_size / Apache LimitRequestBody). max_upload_request_size is NOT a native Mattermost configuration field or API parameter clients must provide: it is the explicit encoded-body budget required by our published jido_chat_mattermost ReqClient and ZAQ planner contract (deps architecture149/196; ReqClient.upload_limit nil=>missing_configuration). Current failure is this local mandatory-budget contract before provider I/O; it does not prove server rejection. SMTP complete MIME ceiling is a distinct requirement. Reassess mandatory handling of absent/unknown Mattermost HTTP budgets against recorded epic/Pages plan before changing contract; do not silently restore adapter orchestration or alter published pins.
